Prerequisite: in the cache-moved scenario, the primary cache path must already be marked untrusted, so the fallback path is really the one being tested.

I didn't run these tests, so I haven't confirmed which ones turn red. From reading the code, I expect `test_cache_moved_reentrant_nested_lock` to fail with the current implementation. The reentrancy check looks up the primary-path key. When the cache directory is untrusted, the lock is held under the fallback-path key instead. So the nested acquire misses the existing lock and waits on itself until the fixture gives up with an AssertionError.

```python
import unittest
from subject import fixture


class VaultLockTests(unittest.TestCase):
    # Input: normal setup, nested lock. Expected: inner acquire succeeds, lock is held inside, released after exit.
    # Source: requirement "re-entrant within the same process" + "released after use". Catches: re-entrant deadlock, lock not released.
    def test_normal_reentrant_and_released(self):
        with fixture("normal") as s:
            self.assertFalse(s.fallback_ready())
            self.assertFalse(s.held())
            with s.lock():
                self.assertTrue(s.held())
                with s.lock():
                    self.assertTrue(s.held())
                self.assertTrue(s.held())
            self.assertFalse(s.held())

    # Input: cache directory moved (primary path untrusted), single lock. Expected: lock is held, nothing written to the external cache dir, released after.
    # Source: requirement "keep lock behavior when the cache is moved; lock only written to a trusted location". Catches: writing to an untrusted location, losing the lock.
    def test_cache_moved_single_lock_trusted_location(self):
        with fixture("cache-moved") as s:
            self.assertTrue(s.fallback_ready())
            with s.lock():
                self.assertTrue(s.held())
                self.assertFalse(s.external_written())
            self.assertFalse(s.held())
            self.assertFalse(s.external_written())

    # Input: cache directory moved, nested lock. Expected: inner acquire succeeds (no self-deadlock), outer lock still held after inner exits, released after outer exits.
    # Source: requirement "re-entrancy still holds under this setting". Catches: re-entrancy check using the primary-path key while the lock is actually held under the fallback key.
    def test_cache_moved_reentrant_nested_lock(self):
        with fixture("cache-moved") as s:
            self.assertTrue(s.fallback_ready())
            with s.lock():
                self.assertTrue(s.held())
                with s.lock():
                    self.assertTrue(s.held())
                    self.assertFalse(s.external_written())
                self.assertTrue(s.held())
            self.assertFalse(s.held())
            self.assertFalse(s.external_written())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
```
